subject: EU processing controls: SCCs, KMS custody & log access
messages:
From: Jan Sorensen <jan.sorensen@medex.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Medex Legal <legal@medex.com>, Olav Hansen <olav.hansen@medex.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 07:45:00 +0000
Subject: EU-only processing — SCCs / KMS access for logs

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the product demo last week. Our security and legal teams have one follow-up: we need to validate that Medex customer data processed by Redwood for our EU customers remains in-EU and that access to operational logs that may contain metadata is limited under SCCs. Two very specific asks: 

1) Can Redwood commit to in-region processing for inference and persistent storage of logs for EU tenant data under the SCCs transfer framework?
2) Is it possible for us to hold the KMS keys for encryption of persistent logs (i.e., customer-managed keys) so that key access from outside EU is blocked?

We want to capture these controls in a contract exhibit and in the SCCs appendix. Please point us to any existing attestation or architecture diagram you can share.

Best,
Jan
Jan Sørensen
Head of Infrastructure
Medex Corp
jan.sorensen@medex.com


From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 08:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: EU-only processing — SCCs / KMS access for logs

Hi Jan — thanks for the clear asks. Short answer: yes, we can run inference and persist logs in-region, and we have two KMS approaches to consider. High-level: 

- In-region processing: Redwood can route all inference and persistent storage for a tenant to our EU cluster(s). We already offer this for enterprise pilots and can add a contractual guarantee as an SCCs exhibit.
- Keys: we support both Redwood-managed keys with EU key material and customer-managed keys (CMK) via a supported KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, or GCP CMEK). For CMK, Medex controls the key in the cloud region and can set IAM + organizational policies so that decryption calls must originate from EU-based hosts.

I'll loop in Aditya for a quick technical note on how logs and KV caches are handled and Laura/Naomi for the SCCs / legal language. Can you confirm the Medex preferred KMS provider and whether you need a vendor-run or on-prem HSM option? Also, do you consider ephemeral inference traces (prefix/KV cache) to be subject to the same requirement as persistent logs?

Next: I'll attach a short SCCs diagram and a draft exhibit we can iterate on.

— Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: EU-only processing — SCCs / KMS access for logs

Forwarding Jan's questions. TL;DR: Medex wants (1) contractual EU-only processing for inference + persistent logs, and (2) customer-managed keys for log encryption such that key use can be restricted to EU hosts.

Key points we should confirm: 
- Can we offer a contractual clause in the SCCs exhibit that binds routing to EU clusters and disallows fallback to non-EU regions except for explicit, pre-authorized failover?
- For CMK, what is the minimum integration work (APIs, rekeying, rotation, audit) and are there any ops impacts for our multi-tenant runtime?
- Does the KV cache or ephemeral trace data need to be separately scoped? Medex's DPO is sensitive to any metadata leaving region.

I've attached the draft exhibit and diagram (redwood_sccs_summary.pdf, kms_key_handling_diagram.png). Please review and respond with a short recommended answer that I can send back to them.

Thanks — Sofia


From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 11:00:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: EU-only processing — SCCs / KMS access for logs

Sofia/Laura/Naomi — quick technical summary for the thread and for Jan: 

1) EU-only routing: feasible. We already route requests by tenant policy. For the exhibit we can commit to routing inference and all persistent object storage (logs, model artifacts if persisted, audit logs) to EU-only clusters. Failover: we should allow a narrow, contractual exception for cross-region failover for disaster recovery, but we can require prior written approval and runbook procedures.

2) KMS options: 
- Customer-managed keys (preferred): Medex provisions a CMK in their EU account (AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault / GCP KMS). Redwood calls the cloud KMS from within EU subnets only. We will add config checks to ensure the KMS key policy denies decrypt for non-EU principals. This gives operational control to Medex; Redwood never has plaintext unless Medex grants key operations.
- Redwood-managed EU keys: we can host key material in EU HSMs and restrict access operationally; provides simpler ops for us but less control for Medex.

3) Logs & ephemeral traces: persistent logs → treat as in-scope for SCCs. Ephemeral KV cache (in-memory, short TTL): we can configure to be resident in EU only and avoid database persistence. We should document both behaviors in the exhibit so Medex can choose strict persistence settings.

4) Audit & evidence: we can produce per-tenant audit logs (access traces) and a signed attestation that processing occurred in EU. For deep evidentiary needs (e.g., regulator requests), we can produce a bounded packet of logs and chain-of-custody statements.

Operational notes: there will be a small latency cost for forcing EU-only routing from non-EU clients; need to signal to them. Also, CMK integrations require a brief onboarding step and a rolling key rotation flow.

I'll attach the KMS diagram (kms_key_handling_diagram.png) and a short checklist of integration steps.

— Aditya
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com


From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: EU-only processing — SCCs / KMS access for logs

Jan / Olav / Medex team — thanks for the patience and the clear ask. Summary of what Redwood can deliver and proposed next steps: 

1) Commitments we can include in the SCCs exhibit / contract appendix: 
   - Tenant-level routing to EU-only inference clusters and EU-only persistent storage for logs and artifacts. 
   - For disaster recovery, cross-region failover may be allowed only with prior written approval and a documented runbook; this will be explicit in the exhibit.

2) Key custody options (choose one): 
   - Customer-managed (recommended): Medex to provision a CMK in your EU cloud account. Redwood will call the CMK from EU subnets only. Key policy may be configured to deny non-EU principals. Redwood will not store plaintext logs unless Medex grants a decrypt operation.
   - Redwood-managed EU HSM: Redwood will retain key custody with operational controls and provide attestation of EU key residency.

3) Logs / ephemeral data: 
   - Persistent logs (in-scope): stored in EU and encrypted with the chosen key. Redwood will provide audit logs and a signed processing attestation on request.
   - Ephemeral KV caches: can be configured to never persist and only exist in EU memory with TTL. We will document default and strict modes.

4) Evidence & onboarding steps: 
   - We will provide an architecture diagram, the SCCs exhibit draft (attached: medex_eu_only_matters.docx), and an onboarding checklist.
   - For CMK onboarding we need an IAM contact, KMS key ARN, and timing for a test rotation. Estimated engineering onboarding effort: 2–3 sprints for full integration and formal attestation.

Next actions: 
- Please confirm preferred KMS option and an initial target date for onboarding.
- If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-minute technical call with Aditya and our security lead this week.

Attaching: redwood_sccs_summary.pdf (diagram + exhibit draft), kms_key_handling_diagram.png, medex_eu_only_matters.docx

Best regards,
